correctness.rationale: For all strictly ordered five-node grids, the odd-input zeroth coefficient is a nonnegative finite exponential sequence of mean zero; its mean-square identity forces full reflection symmetry. Even-input zeroth coefficients give an infinite odd-power cosine bound which allows exactly cyclic orders three and four. Exact quartic derivative formulas show all cosine coefficients nonnegative on the two grids for every integer pair of input/output frequencies. Uniform Fourier-cone reduction handles every continuous positive-definite kernel. Exact symbolic reconstruction and 15,000 finite mode pairs passed; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: The full Otten–Nguyen–Watts paper studies only uniform grids, whereas the new statement classifies all distinct degree-four grids. The closest published variable-node theorem classifies degrees two and three and explicitly excludes degree four. A previously published cosine-only grid result does not imply simultaneous preservation of every Fourier generator; the difference is essential because frequencies 4r+2 enforce cyclotomic restrictions.
